Show a unit square mapped to a parallelogram, vary the matrix to see area scale, and include a sign change to illustrate orientation. Add multiple matrices for quick comparison and a quick 3D wedge analogy.

topic: The Carnot cycle (heat engine)
prompt: I'm studying thermodynamics and want a visualization of the Carnot cycle on a PV diagram. Animate the four steps—isothermal expansion, adiabatic expansion, isothermal compression, adiabatic compression—connect the cycle, and show efficiency via 1 - Tc/Th. Sweep Th and Tc to show changes in work and efficiency, with labeled Q_H and Q_C.

topic: Directional derivatives and the steepest ascent
prompt: I'm teaching undergrads multivariable calculus and want a vivid visualization of directional derivatives and the gradient as the direction of steepest ascent. Show a 3D surface with a point, arrows for several directions, and animate the directional derivative; highlight the gradient as the steepest ascent direction with color by magnitude. Use multiple scenes: 3D view, contour map, and a side profile.

topic: Fourier transform of a Gaussian pulse
prompt: I'm learning Fourier analysis and want to visualize why a time-domain Gaussian becomes a Gaussian in frequency. Show a time-domain Gaussian pulse and its Fourier transform, and animate the scaling of the time-domain width. Include a live plot of |F(ω)| and show how changing the width swaps concentration between time and frequency, with side-by-side views.

topic: The Van der Pol oscillator
prompt: I'm teaching an undergrad nonlinear dynamics course and want a vivid Van der Pol visualization for different mu. Show phase portraits converging to a limit cycle, plus time traces for small and large mu, and a parameter sweep illustrating how relaxation oscillations emerge. Use color-coded trajectories and a zoomed phase-space view.

topic: The wave equation on a vibrating string
prompt: I'm studying the wave equation on a vibrating string and want to see how an initial pluck propagates. Animate two waves moving in opposite directions, reflections at the ends, and the formation of standing waves; then decompose into Fourier modes and show coefficients evolving. Include a pause to compare the physical string with its modal representation.

topic: The Stable Marriage problem (Gale-Shapley)
prompt: I'm teaching an undergrad algorithm course on stable matching. Visualize Gale-Shapley with a small set of men and women and explicit preferences; show proposals, acceptances, and rejections until a stable match forms. Highlight the evolving bipartite graph and compare the men-optimal vs women-optimal outcomes with a brief runtime note.

topic: The Tower of Hanoi recursive solution
prompt: I'm learning recursion and want a clear Tower of Hanoi visualization for n disks. Show the recursive move sequence, highlight each legal move, and display a live move counter; also depict the recursion tree to illustrate how the solution builds from base cases, with a slow-down at the critical step.

topic: The normal (Gaussian) distribution and the empirical rule
prompt: I'm teaching undergraduate stats and want to illustrate the Gaussian and the empirical rule 68-95-99.7. Display the bell curve with shaded areas for ±1σ, ±2σ, and ±3σ, and animate sampling to show the law of large numbers; contrast with a non-Gaussian distribution to emphasize the rule, with a quick note on real-world data.

topic: Polarization of light – rotating polarizer
prompt: I'm studying optics and want to see Malus' law in action with a rotating polarizer. Animate a fixed polarizer and an incident polarized beam, rotate the analyzer and plot transmitted intensity versus angle; also show linear and circular polarization states and a geometric E-field visualization for intuition.

topic: Lotka-Volterra predator-prey cycles
prompt: I'm teaching undergrads in a mathematical biology course and want a vivid visualization of Lotka-Volterra predator-prey cycles. Show the phase-plane with prey on the x-axis and predators on the y-axis, including a closed orbit around the nontrivial equilibrium. Then animate the time series of both populations and demonstrate a small perturbation that shifts the orbit without destroying its cyclic nature.

topic: Gradient descent on a 3D loss surface
prompt: I'm learning optimization and want a visualization of gradient descent on a 3D loss surface. Render a colorful surface with a valley and a ridge, plot the optimizer's path from multiple starting points, and compare different learning rates on convergence and overshoot. Include a projection onto the 2D contour plane and a trace of the path.

topic: Decision tree – splitting on features
prompt: I'm teaching undergrad ML and want a visual that builds intuition for a decision tree. Start with a 2D dataset, illustrate axis-aligned splits on features, show how entropy or Gini splits choose the best split, and reveal how the tree grows depth by depth with pruning options. End with a simple prediction path to emphasize interpretability.

topic: Double pendulum chaotic motion
prompt: I'm learning chaos with a double pendulum and want a dramatic visualization of its motion. Show two linked rods in 3D with real-time angle tracking, display divergence of nearby initial conditions, and include a side-by-side comparison of nearly identical setups to illustrate chaotic sensitivity.

topic: Rotation matrix (2D) rotating a square
prompt: I'm teaching an undergrad course on linear algebra and want a clean geometric visualization of a 2D rotation matrix rotating a square. Animate the square under a parameter sweep of the rotation angle, show the mapping of each vertex, and include axes and a small diagram explaining how basis vectors rotate.

topic: The unit circle and radian measure
prompt: I'm learning trigonometry and want a precise unit-circle visualization with radian measure. Animate an angle accumulating on the circle, display sine and cosine projections, and connect to identities with dynamic chords and a live table of values as the angle increases.

topic: Depth-First Search (DFS) on a graph
prompt: I'm teaching an algorithms course and want a DFS animation on a graph. Present a labeled graph, highlight the recursive exploration and backtracking, visualize the stack behavior, and provide a step-by-step walkthrough of a concrete DFS path with color transitions.

topic: A* pathfinding with a heuristic
prompt: I'm studying AI pathfinding and want to see A* in action on a grid. Visualize the open and closed lists, show the heuristic guiding the search toward the goal, compare with Dijkstra in the same scene, and present the final path with cost labels and a front-line zoom on the frontier.

topic: The Rossler attractor
prompt: I'm teaching undergrads a nonlinear dynamics course and want a vivid visualization of the Rossler attractor. Build a 3D phase-space trajectory with the classic chaotic orbit, color by time, and highlight how the x, y, z coordinates wind together. Include a parameter sweep to show how small changes alter the attractor, with smooth camera pans and close-ups on the spirals.

topic: The cycloid curve (rolling circle)
prompt: I'm learning calculus and want to understand the cycloid generated by a rolling circle. Animate a point on the rim tracing the cycloid, show the circle's center path, and annotate the parametric equations x = r(t − sin t), y = r(1 − cos t). Explain cusps, velocity, and arc-length intuition, and include a side-by-side comparison with a straight-line track.

topic: Fourier synthesis – adding sine waves to build a square wave
prompt: I'm studying signals and want to see Fourier synthesis building a square wave from sine components. Animate partial sums as you add harmonics, highlighting the Gibbs phenomenon near the edges. Show the evolving waveform with color-coded sine terms and a small plot of the error to the ideal square wave, with a quick sweep over the number of terms to show convergence.

topic: Simplifying algebraic fractions with cross-cancellation
prompt: I'm teaching algebra to undergrads and want to illustrate cross-cancellation in rational expressions. Visualize numerator and denominator as factor grids, cancel common factors step by step, and point out traps like canceling non-common factors. Include examples with and without reducible forms and end with a concise general rule and quick practice.

topic: Duffing oscillator and chaos
prompt: I'm teaching nonlinear dynamics and want a vivid visualization of the Duffing oscillator. Show the double-well potential, the forced and damped equation, and compare periodic and chaotic regimes via time series, phase portrait, and a Poincare section. Include parameter sweeps to reveal the transition to chaos and a slow-motion zoom on the changing attractor shapes.

topic: Slope fields for a first-order ODE (dy/dx = x + y)
prompt: I'm learning differential equations and want to explore slope fields for dy/dx = x + y. Build a dense slope-field and overlay several integral curves from different initial conditions, then derive the exact solution y = Ce^x − x − 1 and verify it on the plot. Include interactive steps showing how small changes in initial conditions drift the trajectories.

topic: Saddle points, local minima, and maxima on a 3D surface
prompt: I'm studying optimization geometry and want a 3D surface visualization with saddle points, local minima, and maxima. Animate gradient flow lines and show curvature via Hessian eigenvectors at critical points, labeling each type with color-coded markers, and include examples like z = x^3 − 3xy^2 to illustrate a saddle.

topic: Monte Carlo simulation for estimating Pi
prompt: I'm teaching statistics and want a clear Monte Carlo estimation of Pi. Show random points tossed inside a square with an inscribed circle, track the ratio to approximate Pi, and animate convergence as sample size grows. Include a discussion of variance, confidence intervals, and a quick comparison with the true value.

topic: Secant lines approaching a tangent line (derivative definition)
prompt:
I'm teaching undergrads calculus and want a vivid visualization of the derivative as a limit of secant slopes.
Plot f(x) and, for a fixed x0, a family of secant lines through (x0, f(x0)) and (x0+h, f(x0+h)) with h shrinking to 0.
Show the slopes converging to f'(x0) and draw the tangent line at x0 with that slope; include the limit expression and a zoom on x0 to highlight the convergence.

topic: Partial fraction decomposition graphically
prompt:
I'm learning calculus and want a visual demonstration of partial fraction decomposition for a rational function.
Show the original function, identify its poles, and decompose into simpler fractions A/(x−r1) + B/(x−r2) + … in a dynamic way.
Animate how adjusting coefficients changes the sum to match the original, with a side-by-side comparison of the combined curve and the components, plus a step-by-step algebra breakdown.

topic: Fractal: Sierpinski triangle generation
prompt:
I'm teaching undergrads fractal geometry and want a rich animation of generating the Sierpinski triangle.
Start with a filled triangle, remove the central inverted triangle, then apply the same operation recursively to the three corner triangles.
Show self-similarity at multiple scales, vary iteration depth, and optionally illustrate a quick fractal-dimension visualization.

topic: The Central Limit Theorem with sample means
prompt:
I'm learning probability and want a CLT visualization: repeatedly sample from a non-normal distribution and form the distribution of the sample means.
Animate how the mean distribution becomes increasingly normal as the sample size n grows, with an overlaid true mean and standard error.
Provide a slider to vary n and the parent distribution (e.g., Uniform, Exponential) to compare convergence behavior.

topic: Heap Sort with heapify operations
prompt:
I'm teaching data structures and want a clear, step-by-step Heap Sort visualization.
Show an array as bars, build a max-heap via heapify, then repeatedly extract the max and restore the heap, highlighting swaps and heap-property checks.
Include a binary-heap tree side-by-side and options for slow-motion vs fast-forward to emphasize algorithmic intuition.

topic: Conic sections: parabola, ellipse, and hyperbola generation
prompt:
I'm studying analytic geometry and want a dynamic construction of parabola, ellipse, and hyperbola.
Animate the focus–directrix definitions and show how parameter changes yield the standard forms y^2=4ax, x^2/a^2+y^2/b^2=1, and x^2/a^2−y^2/b^2=1.
Include the cone-slice interpretation or alternative definitions, and highlight eccentricity and focal properties as the shapes morph.

topic: Blackbody radiation and Planck's law
prompt:
I'm teaching undergrads physics and want a clear visualization of Planck's law for blackbody radiation.
Plot spectral energy density versus frequency for several temperatures, with area under each curve representing emitted energy.
Animate the peak shifting to shorter wavelengths with temperature (Wien's displacement), and annotate constants with color-coded curves and optional photon-quantum language.

topic: Volume of revolution (disk/washer method) for a solid
prompt:
I'm learning calculus and want to see disk/washer methods in action for volumes of revolution.
Revolve a region around an axis to form a solid, showing outer and inner radii and the volume integral V=π∫(R^2−r^2) dx, plus a comparison to the disk method.
Use concrete examples like y=√x rotated about the x-axis or a washer with a hole, and animate slicing, rotation, and a parameter sweep of bounds.

topic: Vector addition and scalar multiplication geometrically
prompt: I'm teaching undergrads linear algebra and want a vivid visualization of vector addition and scalar multiplication in the plane. Show vectors as arrows, build sums via the parallelogram rule, and illustrate how scaling by k stretches, flips, or zeroes vectors. I'd like multiple scenes: lay out given vectors, construct the sum, then demonstrate the effect of a moving scalar on a grid and on tip paths. Use color-coded vectors, a dynamic k slider, and a quick side-by-side to verify commutativity.

topic: Euler's method approximation vs. exact solution
prompt: I'm learning numerical methods and want to see Euler's method compared to the exact solution for a simple ODE. Create a side-by-side animation: integrate dy/dt = f(y,t) from t0 to t1 using Euler steps, while plotting the exact solution, with the error evolving in time. Show step-by-step updates, a zoom into the last few steps, and a parameter sweep of step size to illustrate convergence or divergence. Include algebraic display of the truncation error and a legend that ties each curve to its method.

topic: Prime factorization using factor trees
prompt: I'm teaching an intro number theory course and want a vivid factor-tree visualization of prime factorization. Build a number like 360 as a rooted tree, repeatedly splitting composite nodes into two factors until primes remain. Color-code prime leaves and show the multiplicities with a running tally or a bar chart. Start with the base number, then animate each split and highlight the correspondence to the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic.

topic: Green's theorem in the plane
prompt: As a student of vector calculus, I want to visualize Green's theorem in the plane. Animate a closed curve C bounding a region D, show the line integral around C and the double integral over D, and illustrate how the two are equal by adjusting the field, the orientation, and the region. First with a rectangle, then with a wiggly loop that deforms while keeping the same area, and finally a slider to vary the field to see the relationship stay consistent. Include vector field arrows, tangent components, and a live summation of the two expressions.

topic: Euclidean construction of an equilateral triangle
prompt: I'm teaching a geometry lab for undergrads and want a step-by-step Euclidean construction of an equilateral triangle given a segment. Animate compass-and-straightedge style: draw circles with radius AB centered at A and B, locate the intersection as the third vertex, and prove the sides are equal with congruent radii. Include a final clean diagram with the base fixed, and an alternate construction path to reinforce invariants. Provide a short intuition box on why this works, and a quick check of all sides equal.

topic: Polygon interior angle sum formula
prompt: I'm learning geometry and want an animation that derives the sum of interior angles of an n-gon. Construct a generic polygon, triangulate it step by step and show that the sum equals (n-2)·180 degrees, with a live counter counting the total angle from triangles. Include a slider for n to demonstrate several cases, highlight concave vs convex behavior, and a graph of the sum versus n. Emphasize common misconceptions about exterior angles.

topic: Binary Search Tree – insertion and traversal
prompt: I'm teaching data structures to undergrads and want a clear visualization of BST insertion and traversals. Start with an empty tree, insert a given sequence showing the insertion path and parent-child links, then illustrate in-order, pre-order, and post-order traversals with a highlighted visit order and a log window. Include a visualization of comparisons, show shape changes, and add a small interactive prompt to insert another value to see its path.

topic: Reflection across the x-axis and y-axis
prompt: I'm studying symmetry and want to visualize reflections across the x-axis and y-axis. Show a set of points or shapes and map them to their reflections across each axis, animate the mapping, and discuss fixed points and how successive reflections compose. Provide examples with a general curve, a polygon, and a point cloud, with toggles for axis visibility and color-coding original vs image. Include a quick note on preserved distances and an intuitive explanation of why reflections are isometries.

topic: Tiling with regular polygons (tessellations)
prompt: I'm teaching an undergrad geometry course and want a vivid tessellation visualization. Show how regular triangles, squares, and hexagons tile the plane and explain the angle-sum condition at a vertex. Build scenes that color-code polygons, rotate them around a common vertex, and zoom into the tiling to compare feasible vs. impossible patterns. Animate transitions that illustrate why other regular polygons cannot tile alone, with a brief algebraic note on the 360-degree rule. I’d like the pacing to support discussion and include a simple interactive prompt for students to predict outcomes before the animation proceeds.

topic: Counting Sort and Radix Sort visualizations
prompt: I'm learning algorithms and want a clear visualization comparing counting sort and radix sort. Show step-by-step digit/grouping processing, with buckets filling, stable merges, and the final sorted output. Include side-by-side timelines and histograms to emphasize how counts drive work and how base choice affects performance. Add a few small example runs, and include a parameter sweep over input range to illustrate worst-case vs average behavior. I’d like the scene to highlight intuition of stability, linear-time behavior, and practical tradeoffs for teaching purposes.

topic: PCA (Principal Component Analysis) – reducing 2D data to 1D
prompt: I'm teaching a data science undergrad course and want a visual of PCA reducing 2D data to 1D. Show a noisy 2D cloud, the principal axis of maximum variance, and projection of points onto that axis. Animate the reconstruction of the original data from the 1D representation and illustrate the explained variance ratio with a shrinking residual error. Include a comparison of random vs structured data and a 3D view rotating to reveal the eigen-direction in space. I’d like a clean, intuition-forward sequence with optional algebraic captions for the eigenvectors and eigenvalues.

topic: Electromagnetic wave propagation (E and B fields in phase)
prompt: I'm curious about EM waves and want a visualization where E and B fields propagate in phase in free space. Animate sinusoidal E and B vectors perpendicular to the direction of travel, with a common phase at every point along the wavefront. Show the Poynting vector as an energy flux and annotate wavelength, frequency, and impedance shifts for different media. Include a side-by-side comparison of in-phase vs out-of-phase scenarios and a 3D view that follows a ray front advancing in time. I’d like the animation to support discussion of surfacing phase and amplitude relationships for introductory physics students.

topic: Linear regression and the least-squares line
prompt: I'm teaching an undergraduate statistics class and want a visual of linear regression via least squares. Plot noisy data, draw the best-fit line, and animate residuals with their signs and magnitudes to show how the line minimizes error. Demonstrate gradient-descent style updates on slope and intercept, and show R^2 evolving as more data points are added. Include a real-world example, like height vs. weight, with a guided intuition about correlation and prediction intervals. End with a quick recap of normal equations and a visual contrast to robust fits when outliers are present.

topic: Merge Sort – divide and conquer merging
prompt: I'm learning data structures and want a visual of merge sort's divide-and-conquer process. Show subarrays as color-coded bars, with a timeline highlighting each merge operation until a fully sorted array emerges. Include a brief walkthrough of the recursion tree and a quick contrast to quicksort for intuition. I’d like the pacing to emphasize the cost of merging and memory usage via a compact visual footprint.

topic: Gravitational field lines of two masses
prompt: I'm teaching a mechanics course and want a visualization of gravitational field lines from two masses. Animate test particle trajectories along the combined field and highlight regions of stable versus unstable paths. Provide 3D perspectives, and contrast equal-mass and unequal-mass setups with color-coded field strength. I’d like a concise, physically-grounded sequence that builds intuition for superposition and the geometry of gravity.

topic: Random walk in 1D and 2D
prompt: I'm studying stochastic processes and want a visualization of 1D and 2D random walks. Show multiple walkers performing steps with a clear time axis, tracking mean displacement and the spreading cloud. Compare 1D and 2D behavior, include a single long trajectory overlay and an ensemble path ensemble to illustrate diffusion. Add sliders for step size, step distribution, and dimensionality; annotate how the central limit theorem underpins the observed spreading. I’d like a clean narrative that connects random motion to practical diffusion problems in physics or finance.

Add a quick intuition note on why angular speed varies to keep the area constant.

prompt:
I'm studying electrostatics and want to visualize equipotential surfaces around a point charge.

topic: Convection currents in a fluid
prompt:
I'm teaching a fluid dynamics module and want to visualize convection currents in a heated fluid.

topic: K-Means clustering convergence (centroid movement)

topic: Exponential distribution (waiting times)

prompt: I'm teaching calculus to undergrads and want a geometric visualization of the product rule using rectangle areas. topic: The quadratic formula and its discriminant (real vs. complex roots)

topic: Binary search on a sorted array
prompt: I'm studying algorithms and want a visualization of binary search on a sorted array. prompt: I'm teaching undergrads optimization and want a vivid visual of simulated annealing that shows escaping local minima. prompt: I'm teaching an undergrad math course and want a visualization of Lissajous figures generated by x=sin(a t), y=sin(b t) with different frequency ratios. prompt: I'm learning data structures and want a visualization that walks through quicksort partitioning with a pivot. prompt: I'm teaching an undergrad probability course and want a vivid visualization of the law of large numbers with a fair coin. topic: Arithmetic vs. geometric sequences and series
prompt: I'm learning sequences and want to understand the difference between arithmetic and geometric sequences and their sums. Create visuals that compare term growth, partial sums, and convergence behavior side by side, with intuitive narratives and a quick derivation of the sum formulas, highlighting when each series diverges.

topic: Phase transition – melting/freezing at a molecular level
prompt: I'm teaching an undergrad physics/chem course and want a vivid visualization of phase transitions at the molecular level. Show a lattice of particles that melts to liquid as energy is pumped in, include latent heat and order parameters, and move from micro-scale motion to a coarse-grained thermodynamic portrait.

topic: Bifurcation diagram of the logistic map
prompt: I'm studying nonlinear dynamics and want a clean visualization of the logistic map bifurcation diagram, with r sweeping from 0 to 4. Show fixed points, their stability changes, period-doubling cascades, and chaotic regimes, plus zoom-ins around the Feigenbaum point and a few representative orbits to illustrate behavior.

topic: Scaling and shearing transformations
prompt: I'm teaching an undergrad linear algebra and want an animation that builds intuition for scaling and shear transforms in 2D. Animate grids and shapes under these transforms, compare eigen-directions for scaling, and show the effect of composing both operations, with a short derivation of representative transformation matrices.

topic: Correlation coefficient (r) – positive vs. negative vs. zero
prompt: I'm learning statistics and want to visualize how the correlation coefficient r captures linear association. Create three scenes showing positive, negative, and near-zero correlations with scatter plots and best-fit lines, then a visual of how r is computed and how outliers can affect it, finishing with a caution about mistaking causation.

topic: Simple pendulum: small-angle approximation vs. real motion
prompt: I'm teaching an undergrad classical mechanics and want a clear comparison between the small-angle approximation and the real pendulum motion. Show the approximate sinusoidal model versus the exact nonlinear solution, include phase portraits and time-series, and explain where the approximation breaks down as energy grows.

topic: De Broglie wavelength – particle-wave duality
prompt: I'm studying quantum physics and want a visualization of de Broglie wavelength and wave-particle duality. Show a massive particle with a modulated wave packet, relate wavelength to momentum, compare particle trajectories to evolving interference patterns, and demonstrate how confinement changes the wavelength.

topic: Trie data structure for word prefix search
prompt: I'm teaching an undergrad data structures course and want a vivid visualization of a trie for word prefix search. Show inserting a dictionary with common prefixes, then demonstrate prefix queries with dynamic highlighting of shared nodes. I'd like multiple scenes: building the trie, performing lookups, and comparing search times as the dictionary grows. Include intuitive explanations of why tries speed up prefix matching.

topic: Double integrals over a rectangular region
prompt: I'm learning multivariable calculus and want a visual of double integrals over a rectangle. Start with tiling the region with tiny rectangles to approximate the integral, then show how to swap the order of integration (dx dy vs dy dx) and why Fubini's theorem applies. Include a red shading of the integral value as the grid accumulates, and compare edge cases where the bounds are swapped.

topic: Multiplication as repeated addition (grid/array visualization)
prompt: I'm teaching introductory algebra and want a grid visualization that builds multiplication as repeated addition. Show a matrix of unit squares forming a rectangle of size a by b, with each added row colored differently, and animate the total as the grid fills. Include a demonstration of ab as repeated addition and a quick nod to the distributive property via partial grids.

topic: The Pythagorean theorem with square areas on triangle sides
prompt: I'm teaching a geometry class and want a visual proof of the Pythagorean theorem using squares on the triangle sides. Animate constructing on a right triangle: build squares on each leg and hypotenuse, then rearrange pieces to show equal areas. Include a clear geometric intuition and an overlay that highlights how the two leg-squares sum to the hypotenuse-square.

topic: Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) – geometric interpretation
prompt: I'm learning linear algebra and want a geometric interpretation of SVD. Visualize A acting as a rotation and scaling: show V rotating the input, Σ scaling along principal axes, then U rotating to output. Use a concrete 2x2 example and animate how the unit circle maps to an ellipse under A, with the singular vectors as the ellipse axes.

topic: Solving a linear equation (e.g., 2x + 3 = 7) step-by-step
prompt: I'm solving a linear equation and want a step-by-step animation for 2x + 3 = 7. Show subtracting 3 from both sides, then dividing by 2, with checks that x = 2 satisfies the equation. Include a live algebraic balancing display and a quick recap of the general method for ax + b = c.

topic: Entropy and the second law of thermodynamics (visualizing microstates)
prompt: I'm teaching thermodynamics and want a visualization of entropy and the second law through microstates. Show a simple system with many microstates transitioning from low to high multiplicity, animate counting microstates W and plotting S = k ln W over time. Include a comparison of reversible vs irreversible processes and a rising macrostate distribution.

topic: Shell method for volume of revolution
prompt: I'm learning calculus and want to grasp the shell method for volumes of revolution. Visualize building shells around an axis, show the radius and height of each shell, and accumulate volume with a moving cross-section. Compare with the disk/washer method for the same region, and include a 3D perspective of the resulting solid.

topic: De Moivre's theorem and roots of unity
prompt: I'm teaching undergrads in complex analysis and want a vivid visualization of De Moivre's theorem. Show how the nth roots of unity lie at equal angles on the unit circle, then animate z^n mapping to 1 and extract the roots with clear projections. I want scene transitions that vary n (e.g., n=3,4,6) and demonstrate how angles behave under exponentiation.

topic: Hydrogen atom orbitals (1s, 2p, 3d) shapes
prompt: I'm learning quantum mechanics and want to build intuition for the 1s, 2p, and 3d orbital shapes. Visualize |ψ|^2 densities in 3D, with color mapping and cross-sections to show radial nodes; compare spherical 1s to dumbbell 2p along z, and the cloverleaf 3d. Include sliders for exploring r, l, m, and show isosurfaces with labeled nodal regions.

topic: Diffraction through a single slit
prompt: I'm teaching undergraduate optics and want a clear visualization of single-slit diffraction. Animate a plane wave passing through a slit, create wavefronts, then show the intensity pattern on a distant screen with θ; vary slit width a and wavelength λ; highlight minima where a sin θ = m λ with an overlay, and provide a 2D plot of I(θ) alongside dynamic 3D wavefronts.

topic: Bernoulli's principle and a Venturi tube
prompt: I'm learning fluid dynamics and want a visual of a Venturi tube illustrating Bernoulli's principle. Show incompressible flow with a color-coded pressure field and velocity vectors as the fluid passes from wide to narrow sections; add a scenario with different inlet speeds, include a side-by-side plot of P and v along the tube, and annotate the constant along streamlines.

topic: The photoelectric effect (photon energy vs. work function)
prompt: I'm teaching undergrads about the photoelectric effect and want a clear energy diagram and experiments visualization. Show hv vs φ, thresholds, and how electrons are emitted only when hv>φ; animate surface emission with KE = hv − φ, plus a plot of photocurrent vs frequency at fixed intensity, and show how increasing intensity changes saturation current but not the threshold.

topic: Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization process
prompt: I'm studying linear algebra and want a visual walk-through of Gram-Schmidt on three 3D vectors. Show step-by-step projections onto the current basis, subtraction to obtain orthogonal components, then normalization; animate the vectors in 3D space with dot products highlighted and the final orthonormal basis shown in color. Include a concrete numerical example and a quick orthogonality check.

topic: Diffusion of particles (Fick's law)
prompt: I'm teaching physical chemistry and want to visualize diffusion by Fick's law. Use a 2D concentration field with high concentration on the left diffusing to the right; show a color map, flux vectors J = −D ∇C, and the time evolution of C(x,t) solving the diffusion equation; allow parameter sweeps of D and boundary conditions, plus a 1D cross-section plot of C(x,t) over time.

topic: Genetic algorithm – crossover and mutation
prompt: I'm learning about genetic algorithms and want a hands-on visualization of crossover and mutation. Start with a small population of binary strings, show fitness landscape, select parents, perform one- or two-point crossover, apply mutation, and illustrate convergence vs diversity across generations; include a best-fit chart and let the mutation rate be adjustable to see its effect.

topic: Logarithmic functions and their inverses (exponential)
prompt:
I'm teaching undergrads calculus and want a vivid visualization of logarithms as the inverse of the exponential.
Show how y = log_b(x) and y = b^x relate, with a slider to change the base b.
Include two synchronized plots that highlight the inverse relationship, with a point moving along both curves.
Emphasize intuition about domain, range, and how the base changes growth rates.

topic: Hyperbola as a locus of points with constant difference to foci
prompt:
I'm learning analytic geometry and want to see hyperbola as the locus of points with constant difference to two foci.
Build a geometric construction where the foci can move and the set of points updates in real time.
Show the difference of distances to the foci as a fixed value, and illustrate the resulting hyperbola branches.
Include a side plot of distance functions and a quick derivation visual.

topic: Free-body diagram of forces on a block
prompt:
I'm teaching introductory physics and want a clear free-body diagram of a block on a horizontal surface.
Display gravity, normal force, friction, and any external push as vectors, with their directions and magnitudes.
Animate the net force and resulting acceleration, including a scenario with static friction transitioning to kinetic.
Use color coding and labels to reinforce Newton's laws and energy cues.

topic: Graphing sine and cosine waves with phase shifts
prompt:
I'm learning trigonometry and want to see sine and cosine waves with phase shifts visualized vividly.
Animate y = sin(ωt) and y = cos(ωt) with adjustable phase φ, and show how shifting phase moves the graphs relative to one another.
Include a moving point on the unit circle that maps to the wave, plus a time axis that reveals frequency and amplitude.
Provide intuitive explanations for why phase shifts occur in real signals.

topic: Span of a single vector (line) vs. two vectors (plane)
prompt:
I'm teaching linear algebra and want a clear visualization of span in R^2.
Demonstrate that a single vector spans a line through the origin, and that adding a second independent vector spans a plane.
Show a sample point projecting onto the line and the plane as you vary the second vector, with coordinates transforming accordingly.
Include a short note on bases and coordinates to connect visual intuition with algebra.

topic: The Lorentz force on a moving charged particle
prompt:
I'm studying electromagnetism and want a visual of the Lorentz force on a moving charged particle.
Show a particle with velocity v in electric and magnetic fields E and B, and compute F = q(E + v × B) in real time.
Animate the trajectory bending due to the magnetic part and the acceleration from the electric part, with adjustable field strengths.
Provide multiple scenarios, including parallel and perpendicular field configurations, to illustrate drift and gyration.

topic: Adiabatic vs. isothermal expansion
prompt:
I'm teaching thermodynamics and want to compare adiabatic vs. isothermal expansion in a piston.
Plot P–V curves and depict temperature behavior: constant T for isothermal vs rising T for adiabatic, with heat transfer disabled/enabled accordingly.
Animate a gas of particles in the box to visualize energy changes and the work done during expansion.
Include equations PV^γ = const and PV = nRT alongside a narration of the key differences.

topic: Phase portrait for a harmonic oscillator
prompt:
I'm studying differential equations and want a phase portrait for a harmonic oscillator.
Visualize the system with x' = v and v' = -kx - cv, showing how undamped, damped, and critically damped cases differ.
Plot the vector field, sample trajectories from different initial conditions, and highlight conserved energy contours.
Slow down at the turning points and zoom into the origin to reveal the stability structure.

topic: Euler's formula: e^(iθ) = cosθ + i sinθ as a rotating unit circle vector
prompt: I'm teaching an undergrad course on complex numbers and want a vivid visualization of Euler's formula. Animate a unit circle vector rotating by θ, with its real part tracing cosθ and imaginary part tracing sinθ. Show e^{iθ} as the rotating complex arrow and highlight the connection between the components.

topic: Conservation of momentum in 2D collisions
prompt: I'm learning physics and want to see momentum conservation in 2D collisions. Show two bodies approaching and colliding, display their momenta before and after, and illustrate impulse transfer so the total momentum remains constant.

topic: Perceptron decision boundary (linear classifier)
prompt: I'm teaching an undergrad ML course and want a clear visualization of a perceptron deciding in 2D. Plot two classes, draw the linear decision boundary, and animate updates to the weights as misclassified points are corrected.

topic: Brownian motion of a particle
prompt: I'm learning stochastic processes and want to visualize Brownian motion in 2D. Show multiple random paths with small steps, overlay several trajectories, and annotate how the mean square displacement grows over time.

topic: The derivative of x^2 as a visual slope field
prompt: I'm teaching calculus and want to visualize the slope field for y = x^2 with tangent lines. Show a grid of points with tangent lines having slope 2x, and animate a few solution curves to illustrate how they align with the slope field.

topic: Taylor series approximation of sin(x) around 0
prompt: I'm studying series approximations and want to compare sin(x) to its Taylor polynomials around 0. Animate the degree-1, degree-3, degree-5 approximations alongside sin(x), and display the error curve and remainder as x varies.

topic: Elastic vs. inelastic collisions in 1D
prompt: I'm teaching physics and want a side-by-side 1D collision comparing elastic and inelastic cases. Animate two masses colliding on a line, show velocity and kinetic energy graphs, and highlight the energy loss in the inelastic scenario along with the coefficient of restitution.

topic: Laminar vs. turbulent flow visualization
prompt: I'm learning fluid dynamics and want to contrast laminar and turbulent flow in a pipe. Show streamlines and velocity fields under different Reynolds numbers, then transition to chaotic vortex structures to illustrate the onset of turbulence.
